text:
sam: heads-up — onboarding llama3-v2 hit two weird perf symptoms on staging after the safetensors conversion run earlier.
maya: saw this in the profiler too, can you summarize? :eyes:
sam: 1) batcher oscillation: throughput drops every ~20k tokens, latency spikes for P50->P95.
      2) KV cache memcpy CPU time is way up, appears during warmup of long tails.
chris: logs?
sam: pastes: ```
[2026-03-05 14:02:11] batcher: window=8ms -> created batch size=1
[2026-03-05 14:02:11] kernel-select: chosen=matmul_f32_generic (fallback), est_cost=1.8
[2026-03-05 14:02:11] kv-cache: memcpy 48MB, cpu_ms=27.3
[2026-03-05 14:02:31] batcher: window=40ms -> created batch size=12
[2026-03-05 14:02:31] kernel-select: chosen=matmul_q8_opt, est_cost=0.6
```
maya: hmm kernel-select choosing slower FP32 on some requests — why? model metadata says head_dim=64, n_heads=48 but runtime parsed n_heads=32 for some shards.
toni: could be conversion script fallbacking to default n_heads when safetensors metadata is missing.
chris: i repro'd locally: converter warning: "missing 'n_head' in metadata, using legacy default 32" — converter should have failed.
sam: that matches the KV shape mismatch in the trace: "KV shape mismatch expected (48,64) got (32,64)" and then runtime falls back to generic kernels that don't utilize q8 paths.
maya: that explains memcpy spike: mismatched head count -> different KV tensor layout -> runtime copies and reshapes on CPU then uploads.
toni: quick mitigation: add a strict validation check in hfparser to error if n_head/n_embed inconsistent. i'll open a PR.
chris: dev notes: we should also add a lightweight runtime guard that asserts head_dim * n_heads == hidden_size during model load, with a clear error and conversion suggestions.
sam: also for batching oscillation: profiler shows long-tail sequences cause adaptive window to expand then collapse — when a few short-seq requests arrive the batcher snaps to small windows.
maya: suggestion: change adaptive window to track exponential quantiles (e.g., 50th/95th) not just mean, and clamp window changes to avoid thrash.
toni: I'll prototype a 95th-percentile based window and a min-window floor at 8ms. If that stabilizes, we can roll to staging.
infra-bot: deploy: rolling canary started for branch "fix/hfparse-strict-nheads" in cluster staging-a (canary=3pods)
chris: test checklist for PR: - add unit for safetensors metadata missing field -> fail; - add e2e conversion roundtrip test; - record profiler flame before/after.
sam: also add an alert rule: if kernel-select falls back to generic >5% of requests for given model-version -> pager to eng-runtime.
maya: agreed. can we also log "parser-source" tag (checkpoint vs safetensors vs hf) onto model-metadata during onboarding so we can trace back chain?
toni: yep will include that label.
chris: allocation: i'll take the runtime assert, toni takes parser strictness, maya will do batcher quantile prototype, sam will add alert rule + dashboards.
sam: timeline: aim for staging rollout by EOD Friday, revertable if saw perf regressions.
maya: ping me once canary metrics are in; i'll run shadow traffic for 1h.
sam: thanks all :thumbsup:
maya: small follow-up — add converter CLI flag `--require-keys=n_head,n_embd` to fail loudly for ad-hoc runs.
toni: good call.
sam: leaving thread open for canary updates.
infra-bot: monitor: canary metrics: p95 latency - baseline 78ms -> canary 82ms (+5%), generic-kernel-rate 0.9% -> 0.1% after patch applied
sam: nice, looks promising. closing once we confirm 1hr shadow stable.
